questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: A quiz question asks: which substituent increases the acidity of a carboxylic acid most strongly?

options.text: A methyl group at the alpha position
options.misconception: alkyl groups donate and weaken acids

options.text: A nitro group at the alpha position
A methoxy group far from the acid
An amino group as a salt
options.misconception: protonated amino effects are complex but less direct here

questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups such as nitro stabilize the carboxylate conjugate base through induction, lowering the pKa; alkyl groups donate electron density and have the opposite effect.
questions.hint: Withdrawal stabilizes the conjugate base.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the sample reaction, how can a Fischer esterification be driven toward the ester product?

options.text: Using excess alcohol or removing water

questions.explanation: Fischer esterification is an acid-catalyzed equilibrium between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol, so excess alcohol or water removal shifts the position toward ester formation by Le Chatelier's principle.
questions.hint: Remove water or use excess alcohol.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: During a lab exercise, which acyl derivative reacts most rapidly with nucleophiles?

options.misconception: esters are less reactive than acid chlorides

questions.explanation: Acid chlorides are the most reactive acyl derivatives because chloride is an excellent leaving group and the electron-withdrawing chlorine makes the carbonyl highly electrophilic; amides are the least reactive.
questions.hint: Chloride is a great leaving group.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a problem set, what products form when an amide is hydrolyzed under basic conditions?

options.text: A carboxylate salt and an amine
A carboxylic acid and an amine
options.misconception: base gives the carboxylate, not the acid

questions.explanation: Basic hydrolysis of an amide gives a carboxylate salt and a free amine because the hydroxide attacks the carbonyl and the resulting carboxylic acid is deprotonated under the basic conditions.
questions.hint: Base gives carboxylate plus amine.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Testing your understanding: which mechanistic sequence describes reaction of an ester with a nucleophile?

options.text: A single concerted substitution at carbon
Addition to the carbonyl followed by loss of a leaving group

questions.explanation: Nucleophilic acyl substitution proceeds by addition of the nucleophile to the carbonyl to give a tetrahedral intermediate, followed by collapse with expulsion of the leaving group to regenerate the carbonyl.
questions.hint: Addition then elimination via tetrahedral intermediate.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: A problem asks: what product forms when a nitrile is hydrolyzed under aqueous acidic conditions?

options.text: An amide only and no further
options.misconception: acidic hydrolysis proceeds to the acid

questions.explanation: Nitriles hydrolyze under aqueous acid or base through an amide intermediate to give a carboxylic acid, or its salt under basic conditions, with the nitrogen ultimately departing as ammonium or ammonia.
questions.hint: Nitrile hydrolysis ends at the acid.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: An examiner asks: which reagent reduces a carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol?
questions.explanation: Lithium aluminum hydride is strong enough to reduce carboxylic acids to primary alcohols, delivering hydride to the carbonyl after initial deprotonation of the acidic proton.
questions.hint: Lithium aluminum hydride reduces acids.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a handout exercise, which structural motif defines a carboxylic anhydride?

options.text: Two acyl groups joined by an oxygen
An acyl group bonded to chlorine
An acyl group bonded to an alkoxy group
An acyl group bonded to nitrogen

questions.explanation: An anhydride has the motif R-C(=O)-O-C(=O)-R, with an oxygen bridging two carbonyl groups, making it reactive but generally less so than an acid chloride.
questions.hint: Anhydride means two acyls sharing an oxygen.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Applying the mechanism, why does base-catalyzed ester hydrolysis proceed essentially to completion?

options.text: The alcohol is removed by distillation
The carboxylate product cannot be attacked by the alcohol
The ester is more stable than the acid

questions.explanation: Saponification is driven forward because the carboxylic acid formed is immediately deprotonated to a carboxylate, which is not electrophilic toward the alcohol, so the reverse esterification cannot occur.
questions.hint: Carboxylate cannot re-form the ester.
